thread:
alex: Mateo (customer) flagged prod 401s immediately after we rotated their API key. hitting 401s from multiple pods. error: {"code":401,"msg":"invalid_api_key"}. Mateo says previous key worked until rotation window at ~02:15 UTC.

mateo: Confirmed — we rotated via our CI pipeline (helm -> vault kv put), then deployed. Some calls succeed (~5%) and the rest fail. No app code change.

alex: OK, adding infra folks. Priya can you look at Vault/KMS propagation and any helm/ci oddities?

priya: Looking. Quick things to check: 1) vault kv path used by CI vs deployed sidecar (same path?) 2) helm values — key name changed? 3) sidecar env caching / inotify not triggered.

jing: Also check ingress/nginx or CDN caching for Authorization header rewriting? but since 5% success it's probably client/proxy sticky to old pod.

priya: Running quick checks — can you run a curl from an affected pod and paste headers/logs?

mateo: Here's a failing curl from one of their pods:

mateo: ```
$ curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_OLDKEY" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example.com
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_OLDKEY
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

priya: Thanks. Can you also paste vault kv list output from the CI job that wrote the secret? sometimes CI writes to a different subpath (eg -prod vs prod/).

ci-deploy: CI job log snip: `vault kv put secret/redwood/keys/prod api_key=sk_live_NEWKEY` — job reported success and returned 204.

priya: Checking Vault audit logs for KMS unwrap and rewrap timestamps... vault-bot: found write at 2024-07-14T02:15:18Z to secret/redwood/keys/prod by ci-deploy-job-34. KMS unwrap success.

priya: Now checking pods — I see env var in two pod revisions: POD A has ENV API_KEY=sk_live_OLDKEY (stale), POD B has API_KEY=sk_live_NEWKEY. Rolling update didn't fully replace all pods; some older pods remained on the old ReplicaSet due to a missing label update in the helm values.

jing: That explains 5% success — traffic is split between old and new pods. Why didn't kube replace them? Any automated pod restarts?

priya: The helm chart used by CI sets `spec.template.metadata.labels.release: prod-20240714` but our prod cluster's deployment selector was still matching `prod-20240713` because the chart didn't update the selector labels (helm hooks prevented altering selector). So old RS remained.

alex: So client calls hitting old pods with revoked key get 401. Can we force restart old pods as mitigation?

priya: Yes. Mitigation plan: 1) kubectl rollout restart deploy/prod-api — to ensure env reload; 2) confirm pod API_KEY env value equals Vault value: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- printenv | grep API_KEY` ; 3) for immediate, add a short-lived allow rule in auth service to accept the new key mapped to same tenant while we finish the rollout.

mateo: We restarted pods and 401 rate dropped to 0-1%. Good.

alex: What was root cause? Was it Vault propagation, CI, or helm?

priya: Root cause: CI correctly wrote the new key to Vault at secret/redwood/keys/prod. However the Helm release used by CI did not update deployment selector labels (selector immutability + helm hooks), so some old ReplicaSet pods never received the new env var; they continued serving traffic with the old (now-revoked) key. Secondary factor: our canarying logic sent ~10% traffic to older RS during a partial canary which we believed had been drained.

jing: Also noted a minor thing — one old pod had a trailing newline in the env var (helm template had `| n` encoding issue) which caused HMAC mismatch in the auth layer in rare cases. Fixed in the chart.

priya: Action items: 1) Add a CI pre-check to verify helm will update pod template labels or perform a controlled restart when selectors are immutable. 2) Add a post-rotation healthcheck that queries `/health` with new key from multiple pods to ensure no stale pods. 3) Fix helm value templating to strip trailing newlines. 4) Add a short canary draining window and automatic hard restart if stale keys detected.

alex: Mateo, will you validate with your client traffic and confirm stable?

mateo: Confirmed stable for 20m. No more 401 spikes. Thanks.

alex: Closing on our side but adding incident follow-up doc.

priya: I'll open a follow-up ticket and reference CI job logs + helm diff. Also will add a script to `infra/ops` to detect mismatched env values across pods.

jing: FYI we added a temporary alert: `auth.key-drain-failure` if >1% of requests error with invalid_api_key for >5m during rotation windows.

alex: Nice. Summary for ticket: rotated key wrote to Vault successfully, deployment did not fully replace old pods due to immutable selector mismatch in helm chart; stale pods continued using revoked key causing 401s; mitigation: rollout restart and pod env validation; follow-ups: CI checks, helm templating fix, post-rotation healthcheck. :white_check_mark:

mateo: Thanks team. Appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
